The legal precedents mentioned in the text are Smith v. Maryland and Jones v. United States. Smith v. Maryland established the third-party doctrine, which holds that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy for information voluntarily shared with third parties. Jones v. United States applied this principle, referencing Smith to uphold the same idea. The similarity to the case at hand (assuming the "case at hand" refers to the scenario described in the text) is that both cases deal with the third-party doctrine and the lack of a reasonable expectation of privacy for information given to third parties.

The largest country in the world is Russia.
